mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when unemployment is low, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% may signal monetary tightening, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, thus causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive when the federal funds rate is above 2.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both unemployment rate and payroll employment suggests conflicting labor market signals, which may lead to market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive when both unemployment and payroll employment increase, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP indicates economic contraction, which may lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive when GDP is declining, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a strong supply chain, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when industrial production is increasing, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index above 215 indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive when CPI is above 215, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales suggests strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when both housing starts and retail sales increase, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate in a late-cycle expansion indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when unemployment is low in a late-cycle expansion, this hypothesis is falsified.
